niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why Nobody Noticed Your Mistake
ideas.angle: The video reveals that others notice our flaws 50% less than we think due to the Spotlight Effect. It uses generic city footage of crowds to show how everyone is focused on themselves, not you.

hook.en: Nobody is actually looking at you.

ideas.reason: Search interest in social anxiety and 'main character syndrome' is peaking. This provides a psychological 'relief' that encourages saves and repeats.
sources: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (Gilovich, Medvec, and Savitsky, 2000)

ideas.title: Why Your Brain Won't Shut Up
ideas.angle: It explains the Zeigarnik Effect—why unfinished tasks haunt your thoughts while finished ones are forgotten. It shows how 'open loops' create mental tension that keeps you awake.
ideas.reason: The 'productivity' and 'sleep' niches are massive. Explaining the 'why' behind a common frustration like 'racing thoughts' drives high engagement.
sources: Bluma Zeigarnik (1927) Research on Task Interruption

ideas.title: The Secret to Making People Like You
ideas.angle: This flips social logic by explaining that people like you more after they do YOU a favor. It uses the Ben Franklin Effect to show how the brain justifies its actions through cognitive dissonance.

hook.en: Want someone to like you? Ask for a favor.

ideas.reason: Counter-intuitive social 'hacks' perform exceptionally well in the 'dark psychology' and self-improvement sub-niches on YouTube Shorts.
sources: Jecker and Landy (1969) study on liking
